hook: Go in knowing that this file is unusually aware of you, the person reading it. Stray digits keep turning up inside words, and a garbled line of capitals sits at the very top; resist the urge to skim past them. It is short and reads best in one sitting, start to finish, with a little profanity near the end.
whyItMatters: SCP-2357 is one of the pages where the report format itself becomes the anomaly: the object is not something in a locker but the text in front of you, so reading is the containment problem. It takes a familiar Foundation idea, information that is dangerous to know, and turns it toward flattery instead of harm. That makes it a sharp, compact study in how much an SCP file can do with its own conventions.
thingsToNotice:
The file is a proof of concept: its author, Dr. Vanessa Graff, built a document that makes every qualified reader admire it, pass it to the people around them, and refuse to edit or write anything else about it, so the 'containment' of framed copies in every office is simply the spread it causes. The addendum reveals it as a resignation letter written after she has already defected to a rival group, angry that a neuroscientist director dismissed her memetics proposal and that her peers backed him.

The stray digits are only ever 2, 3, 5 and 7, the item number, and they cluster where the text strains, most loudly when she quotes her boss calling the idea impossible. The top line, once the digits are read as letters, is German asking you to ignore the memetic frame. The footnote explains that the failsafe against sanitizing the file leaves some details permanently wrong, which casts doubt on the friendly object class and on every reassurance in the report. Her parting note, that she could easily have killed everyone and chose not to, is the real warning she wants the Foundation to hear.
